content: A spoken language is a natural form of human communication in which words are articulated through the use of the mouth. The majority of human languages fall under the category of spoken languages. Spoken communication is distinct from sign language and written language. From the perspective of linguistic evolution, spoken language predates written language. Writing systems for any given language are developed or invented by its users as a means to record speech when the necessity arises. Even in the modern era, there are numerous languages around the world that exist solely in spoken form and lack a standardized written system. Individuals with the ability to hear typically acquire their first language through spoken communication, while the skill of writing is learned at a later stage. In the field of linguistics, spoken language provides insight into many authentic features of human speech, whereas written language is considered a revised or secondary representation of speech. Consequently, linguists primarily rely on data derived from everyday spoken language for their research and analysis, as it is regarded as the most authentic form of linguistic expression. From a syntactic perspective, spoken language often possesses its own unique set of grammatical structures, which can sometimes differ significantly from those found in written language. Similarly, sign languages share the same natural origins as spoken languages and exhibit comparable levels of grammatical complexity. However, sign languages utilize the hands, arms, and facial expressions as their primary means of articulation, rather than the oral structures used in spoken language.
